content.intro: Learn handling view errors through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Handling View Errors matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines handling view errors as part of url routing and views. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Http404; PermissionDenied; Returning appropriate error responses; Custom error handling; Keeping sensitive internal details out of public errors. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Http404
items.text: Http404 is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: PermissionDenied
items.text: PermissionDenied is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

items.title: Returning appropriate error responses
items.text: Treat Returning appropriate error responses as a reproducible diagnostic: capture the exact input and observed result, isolate one hypothesis, and add a regression test once the cause is fixed. Avoid exposing internal stack traces or secrets to public users.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
